newsitem.title: GREECE: Greenpeace blocks oil refinery in Greece.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace blocks oil refinery in Greece.

text.p: Greenpeace activists on Tuesday blocked the port facilities for Greece's largest oil refinery, the Motor Oil facilities which are joint-owned by Saudi Aramco and the Vardinoyannis family, alleging they were unsafe.
Greenpeace speedboats manoeuvred to stop tankers from arriving or leaving and the Greenpeace ship Arctic Sunrise docked at one of the loading berths, reporters at the scene said.

"We will stop all docking to load or unload until the government pledges to apply safety laws and to stop loading at night or during heavy seas," Greenpeace spokesman Stelios Tsomas told reporters at the scene.
Greenpeace activities also chained themselves to buoys and unfurled a giant red banner proclaiming "Stop Oil". Three tankers were docked at the facility.

The Saudi Arabian Oil Company, Aramco, bought a 50 percent stake in the Vardinoyannis family's Motor Oil Corinth Refineries SA and the accompanying Avinoil Industries distribution network in Greece for $379 million earlier this year.
The Corinth refinery has an annual capacity of 4.5 million tonnes.
No one was available at Motor Oil for immediate comment.
